findings.description: Direct inspection of all five V192 views and six pose renders: the neutral skirt front is smoother than V190, but the waist-to-skirt junction remains ragged and the skirt reads as uneven, narrow vertical folds. In crouch and sit, the apron still falls between/behind the legs with broad anterior thighs exposed. The silhouette and pose coverage remain unacceptable.

V192 front, side, three-quarter, and prone views still show angular planar folds across the bodice, a gray waist patch with unverified garment-surface ownership, and a stiff irregular waist/back transition. Bodice appearance remains unacceptable.

V192 independently scaled four canonical front panels and anchored 108 authored front-lap hem vertices plus 262 shared panel-boundary vertices. Orientation-safe scales were overskirt-front-lap-left 0.0065, overskirt-front-lap-right 0.0242, overskirt-front-left 0.0580, overskirt-front-right 0.1036; mean effective blend was 0.0246 and maximum rest displacement 0.0051 m. Distinct anterior-thigh ray hits were 51/532 in crouch and 21/532 in sit (V190: 50/532 and 21/532). Slight geometric change did not close exposed thigh regions; these diagnostics are not fit acceptance.
